en: Jātaka: The Sixth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Son of the Harsh Man (Kharaputtavagga)
1. The Kharaputtajātaka:
"Truly, as the wise have said, 'The fool is clothed in darkness.'"
“Behold the fool who,
revealing his secret deed, does not wake up.
“You too, my friend, are a fool.”
"Kharaputta, understand this:
he is indeed encircled by a rope,
with his neck bent and his face cast down."
Furthermore, friend, it is childishness on your part that you do not flee when you are free; indeed,
friend, you are even more childish than that.
“Senaka, whom you carry,
I am indeed a fool; O King,
please understand me as such.”
"Now, tell me when asked, by what means was Senaka a fool?
"Having attained the highest goal,"
He who would betray his wife will thereby destroy himself,
and she shall no longer be his.
“O Lord of Men, such a person does not truly love what is dear;
having disregarded his own self, he pursues things that are merely dear to him.
One’s own self is better, and one’s own self is supreme.”
"Can those who are dear be obtained later by one who has practiced the true goal?
Thus ends the first Jātaka, the Kharaputtajātaka.
